page.layout: One page of text in a single column; a small note block below the italic passages, set in smaller type; a catchword "Si" at the lower right. No margin notes beside the column.

main_text.p: quod etiam uefica contingit affecta. Sed si febris fuerit, & urinæ cruditas fuerit, & urinarum cruditas, uitium est corporis totius: sunt enim laminæ huiusmodi, si Galeno credimus, superficiales partes uasorum resolutorum, & quæ contabuerunt. Si uero febris non fuerit, & urinæ coctio fuerit, & dolor, uitium est uesicæ.

p.i: Pultacea seu farina hordei crasiori si-milis, quæ Græcè crimnodes, id est, quæ crimna, hoc est, grandiusculas effractihordei impolentis rectas partes, ob inexquisitam in mola domitu-ram, repræsentat:
b. Vehementem partium solidarum colliqua tionem.

main_text.p: a. b. Si candida fuerit, solidæ partes colliquatur: si rubra, sanguis affatur autore Aetio.
a. b. Primum constat ex tertio tertij epidemiorum ægro. Secundum ex primo primi epidemiorum Sileno.

page.notes: Marginal fragments of the facing page show through faintly and are not transcribed. Greek words "crimnodes" and "crimna" are transliterated as printed in Greek letters in the scan (κρίμνον style) but rendered here in Latin letters as they are the printed text; the Greek ligature forms were not clearly legible.
